jobs.feedName: Michael D. Eisner College of Education
jobs.title: High School English Teacher at Henderson Collegiate
jobs.description: Employer: Henderson Collegiate Expires: 11/28/2026 Do you have a passion for literature? Do you enjoy helping others interpret the meaning of texts? We are looking for a High School English Teacher to help our students cultivate a love of reading, analyze texts and prepare for college. Each English teacher at Henderson Collegiate is assigned an instructional coach to help you navigate the complexities of leading a classroom and teaching rigorous content. In addition to being observed by your coach regularly, you would also meet with them one on one to help develop your teaching skills and close student gaps in understanding. English courses introduce students to a variety of texts and help students to analyze and write about their analysis. To further support you as an English teacher, you would be part of a school-wide department that ensures continuity as students progress from year to year to help students develop the skills and habits that set them up for success in upcoming courses and in college. Applicants should have a bachelor's degree, but do not need a degree in education. Salary ranges between $48,000 and $86,000 depending on level of education and experience. This is an opening for our 2027-28 school year and new teachers will begin in mid July.Who We AreHenderson Collegiate is a mission-driven public college preparatory school located in rural Henderson, NC with an unrelenting focus on character development and student achievement. We believe in 51% character and 49% academics, as we will never sacrifice a moment to teach our students character traits that will help them become great people.Our school serves students that come from traditionally underserved communities (approximately 85% receive free or reduced-price meals, and about 94% are students of color). However, we consistently rank in the top 9.7% of all NC schools and the top 1.3% of all NC Title I schools. Henderson Collegiate is committed to the idea that all students can learn and create a future for themselves that is full of opportunities. We know they can do this by attending and graduating from the colleges of their choice. Our students are proving what is possible and to date, 100% of our seniors have been accepted into a 4-year college or university.We are both a team and family who leverage passionate people to be the best teachers and leaders that they can be. We believe in the idea that all of our staff members are school teachers, as opposed to classroom teachers, meaning that no matter your role, we are all willing to do whatever it takes to support all Henderson Collegiate students. We work together to make what most people say is impossible, happen.Who You AreA go-getter that will move mountains to do what is best for our students and team An encourager who knows that with learning comes joy, love and laughter A reflective educator who recognizes the power and potential within all students and strives to provide them with culturally competent/responsive instruction A life-long learner that continuously strives to be a better version of themselves through learning, improving and being hungry for feedback A gritty problem-solver who approaches challenges with smart solutions in mind A finisher who plans backwards to meet timelines and manage complex projects and who keeps in mind both the big picture and the details necessary to make things happen A data-driven analyst who reflects and takes swift action based on results A proactive communicator who reaches out to students, families, and teammates What You’ll DoBring it. Have stamina and the ability to set and achieve ambitious goals, and handle the intensity required to bring your best self to an extended school day in a very high-performing school environment. Own and develop your own content and curriculum. Do the intellectual preparation needed to create and develop rigorous assessments, unit plans, lesson plans, and instructional materials; demonstrate expertise in and a genuine passion for curriculum that is contagious to students. Deliver strong. Dynamically lead students in whole-class and small-group settings, cultivate intellectual curiosity and a love of learning in students, and adjust instruction using qualitative and quantitative data to ensure student understanding and meet differentiated student needs. Reach higher – and sweat the small stuff. Develop, uphold, and implement Henderson Collegiate’s values, policies, and systems to effectively manage a classroom and consistently lead students to meet sky-high academic and character-based expectations. Never stop growing. Offer and receive constructive feedback from colleagues in order to create a professional working atmosphere that aspires to excellence and is conducive to constant improvement; dive humbly into school-wide and individual professional development, including pre-service training over the summer and weekly sessions during the academic year. Spread the love. Build deep relationships with students, families, and staff to foster a culture of joy and community. Maintain strong lines of communication with families about student progress, and go above and beyond to support and collaborate closely with teammates in the united pursuit of Henderson Collegiate’s mission. The Fine PrintRequired: All candidates must have a Bachelor’s degree. Preferred: Prior experience teaching and working in a low-income community is preferred but not required. Benefits: Salary is competitive and commensurate based on experience, our teacher pay scale can be found here. Additionally, Henderson Collegiate offers a full benefits package. Teachers receive a laptop computer and are provided with classroom technology and software. We believe in going the extra mile for students and as a result our school day is longer than many other schools. The school day for staff is from 7:20 am to 4:15 pm, with one day a week staff being expected to stay until 5:00pm for professional development. At this time we are not able to sponsor candidates who are looking for an initial US work visa.

jobs.title: Licensed Clinician – Adult ID/DD Residential & Day Services at Work Inc
jobs.description: Employer: Work Inc Expires: 11/28/2026 Licensed Clinician – Adult ID/DD Residential & Day ServicesJob Title: Licensed Clinician – Adult ID/DD Residential & Day Services Department: Clinical Services Reports to: VP of Clinical Services Effective Date: 10/28/26Job Summary The Licensed Clinician provides independent, consultative clinical support to adult residential and community-based programs serving individuals with intellectual and developmental disabilities, including those with complex behavioral and mental health needs. Clinicians play a key role in the development, implementation, and monitoring of Positive Behavioral Intervention Supports (PBIS) in alignment with DDS regulations and best practice standards, ensuring behavioral supports are person-centered, rights affirming, and clinically sound.This role offers a high degree of professional autonomy, allowing clinicians to exercise clinical judgment in conducting assessments, developing Functional Behavioral Assessments and Behavior Support Plans when indicated, and guiding residential teams in consistent, ethical implementation. Clinicians work across assigned clusters and programs, balancing direct clinical involvement with mentorship, consultation, and systems-level collaboration to promote regulatory compliance, staff competency, and positive outcomes for individuals.The ideal candidate is comfortable working within adult residential settings, understands the clinical and regulatory complexities of supporting adults with ID/DD, values interdisciplinary teamwork, and is motivated by helping individuals live safer, more fulfilling lives through evidence-based, PBIS-informed, and person-centered approaches.Duties and Responsibilities Clinical Assessment & Intervention • Provide direct clinical support to adults with ID/DD within residential and day programs • Conduct Functional Behavioral Assessments (FBAs) and develop individualized Positive Behavior Support Plans grounded in PBIS and trauma-informed care • Monitor effectiveness of behavior support strategies and adjust plans collaboratively with teams Consultation, Training & Mentorship • Serve as a clinical consultant to residential and day program staff, supervisors, and interdisciplinary teams • Provide hands-on coaching and training to ensure fidelity of behavior support plans • Mentor and support newer or less experienced clinicians • Support the planning, delivery, and ongoing evaluation of PBIS, Safety Care, and incident reporting trainings for new hires and existing staff across programs. Collaboration & Systems-Level Work • Facilitate Universal Cluster Team meetings and contribute to Tier II/Tier III clinical review processes • Participate in Human Rights Committee and Peer Review meetings as a clinical representative • Collaborate with families, DDS staff, DPPC, and community partners to ensure coordinated care Required Skills and Abilities • Strong understanding of adult intellectual and developmental disabilities, including co-occurring mental health diagnoses • Ability to apply behavioral and counseling frameworks in real-world residential settings • Comfortable providing clinical guidance to direct care staff with varied levels of experience • Skilled at balancing structure with flexibility in dynamic environments • Confident communicator who can translate clinical concepts into practical strategies • Sense of humor, patience, and resilience when supporting complex individuals Education and Experience • Master’s degree in Social Work, Counseling, Psychology, Behavior Analysis, Special Education, or related field • Independent or associate licensure preferred (LICSW, LCSW, LMHC, or BCBA); candidates actively pursuing licensure • Minimum of 2 years of clinical experience, with preference for experience in adult residential or community-based ID/DD services • Demonstrated comfort working with individuals with complex behavioral or mental health needs • Valid Massachusetts Driver’s License and ability to travel between program sites

Our core values guide our work, ensuring that each child we serve is treated with dignity and respect. abilities can learn and grow at their own pace.Incorporating fun and engaging learning experiences into every therapeutic service provided to promote a positive and enriching environment.Collecting sit on the floor or stand for extended periods of time.Must be willing and able to hold/transport and utilize quick body movements as indicated in the Behavior Intervention Plan in the course of jobs.description: Employer: Helen Keller Services Expires: 11/28/2026 Teacher of Visually Impaired - Related Services ClinicianRegular Full-TimeCLC – Islandia and Plainview NY Salary: $75-85K Since 1893, Helen Keller Services (HKS) has been committed to improving the lives of individuals who are blind, visually impaired, or have combined hearing and vision loss. HKS serves in the New York City/Long Island area from its new headquarters in dynamic downtown Brooklyn and the Helen Keller National Center for Deaf-Blind Youth and Adults of Sands Point, New York, which has a network of regional offices that extends HKS' reach across the United States. Helen Keller Services for the Blind is thrilled to announce we will be expanding our Children's Learning Center to two brand-new Long Island locations in Nassau and Suffolk County! These state-of-the-art facilities will serve preschool children who are blind or have low vision, as well as multiple disabilities, autism, Down syndrome, or pervasive developmental delays. This expansion reflects HKSB’s commitment to ensuring that Long Island families have access to the same high-quality early education and support services that have transformed lives in our Brooklyn Children Learning Center. We currently have an exciting opening for a Teacher of the Visually Impaired – Related Services Clinician in our soon to open Suffolk and Nassau County Preschools! The TVI – Related Services Clinician will work in the CLC’s preschool program providing one-to-one and small group sessions with preschool children who have special needs and whose IEP mandates vision-related services. The role also involves creation and recording of daily session notes, quarterly/annual report writing, data tracking, and all other documentation related to the position. Specific responsibilities will include: Provide direct instruction to students in individual, small-group, and classroom settings through both pull-out and push-in service models. Collaborate with classroom staff and related service providers to develop and implement adaptations, accommodations, and instructional strategies to meet individual student needs. Adapt materials, learning environments, and instructional methods to support student access, participation, communication, and independence. Support the development of communication, visual efficiency, sensory, cognitive, social-emotional, and adaptive skills through individualized instruction and intervention. Maintain timely, accurate, and compliant documentation, including session notes, progress monitoring, assessment results, service records, quarterly reports, annual reviews, IEP-related documentation, and other required program records. Conduct and contribute to functional vision assessments, learning media assessments, and other vision-related evaluations, as appropriate. Interpret vision reports and incorporate vision-related recommendations into educational programming. Support implementation of IEP goals and monitor student progress through ongoing assessment and data collection. Provide consultation, training, and guidance to school staff and families regarding effective strategies for supporting students with visual impairments. Maintain timely and accurate documentation, service records, progress reports, and required program data. Participate in IEP meetings, multidisciplinary team meetings, parent conferences, and educational planning activities. Respect and support family participation in educational planning and decision-making. Maintain New York State certification requirements for Teachers of Students with Blindness and Visual Impairments (All Grades). Maintain a professional demeanor and contribute positively to the school community and work environment. Services will be provides across Suffolk and Nassau schools as needed. Responsible for other duties as may be assigned or requested by his/her immediate supervisor and/or the Director of the Department. EDUCATION and/or EXPERIENCE REQUIRED EDUCATION/EXPERIENCE NYS Certification: Blind and Visually Impaired (All grades) required Bachelor’s Degree from accredited program required, Master’s Degree preferred Students with Disabilities (B-2 or all grades), in addition to Blind and Visually Impaired Teacher certification or extension preferred Experience working with students in a 4410 preschool setting is preferred CERTIFICATES, LICENSES, REGISTRATIONS New York State certified Teacher of Visually Impaired PHYSICAL DEMANDS The employee is required to safely lift, assist, and transport children, including lifting up to approximately 30 pounds, as required for daily care, positioning, and use of equipment. jobs.title: Manager of Youth & Student Learning at Museum of the Shenandoah Valley
jobs.description: Employer: Museum of the Shenandoah Valley Expires: 11/28/2026 The Museum of the Shenandoah Valley (MSV) is seeking a creative, collaborative, and engaging Manager of Youth & Student Learning to connect pre-K–12 students, youth, families, teachers, and school communities with the Museum’s collections, exhibitions, historic sites, gardens, and natural resources.In this role, you will create opportunities for young learners to explore, ask questions, and discover something new through student field trips, hands-on workshops, guided experiences, family programs, and outreach. You will also support teachers through professional development and resources that extend learning before and after a Museum visit.Reporting to the Director of Education, you will lead youth and student program development and management, build relationships with schools and community partners, coordinate program operations and budgets, and use educator and participant feedback to strengthen future programming. What You’ll Own:Collaborate with the Director of Education, Manager of Adult Learning, and colleagues to develop the annual Education Department programming plan, calendar, priorities, and goals.Develop, coordinate, teach, and evaluate programs for pre-K–12 students, youth, families, teachers, and school communities, both on campus and through outreach and off-site experiences.Create standards-informed curricula, lesson plans, and age-appropriate learning experiences inspired by MSV collections, exhibitions, historic sites, gardens, natural resources, and regional history and culture.Develop pre-visit and post-visit materials, teacher resources, and hands-on experiences that support learners with diverse backgrounds, learning styles, abilities, and needs.Build relationships with teachers, school administrators, homeschool communities, youth-serving organizations, and community partners; develop teacher professional development and educator workshops.Collaborate with Arts & Education colleagues on interpretive, interactive, and hands-on materials for school programs, exhibitions, galleries, and family engagement.Oversee program logistics with the Education Coordinator and appropriate staff, including reservations, schedules, group capacity, materials, supplies, space use, audiovisual needs, and staffing.Manage assigned program budgets and expenses with the Director of Education; train, mentor, and provide program-specific guidance to part-time Educators and select volunteers.Coordinate with colleagues on program planning, promotion, staffing, and support; evaluate attendance, participation, teacher and student feedback, and program quality to inform improvements.Support MSV Makerspace programming and operations, adult programs, and other Education Department initiatives; explore digital and virtual learning resources, pursue professional development, and perform other duties that advance the organization. What You Bring:We’re looking for someone who combines thoughtful program design with strong teaching, organization, and a welcoming approach to learning. The ideal candidate enjoys working directly with children and youth and helping educators and families connect with the Museum.Minimum qualifications include:Bachelor’s degree or an equivalent combination of education and relevant experience in education, museum education, art education, museum studies, public history, history, humanities, or a related field.At least two years of relevant experience developing and facilitating educational programs for children, youth, students, families, or teachers.Experience developing curriculum, lesson plans, school programs, field trips, or other learning experiences for pre-K–12 audiences.Experience working directly with children and youth in formal or informal learning environments and communicating effectively with teachers, caregivers, and school or community partners.Familiarity with academic standards and museum education practices, including inquiry-based, object-based, experiential, and hands-on learning approaches.Proficiency with Microsoft Office/Microsoft 365 and comfort with, or the ability to learn, audiovisual systems, registration systems, digital learning platforms, and other program technology.Preferred qualifications include:Master’s degree in a relevant field.Experience in a museum, historic site, school, arts organization, or similar cultural or nonprofit institution.Knowledge of, or interest in developing knowledge of, Shenandoah Valley history, culture, art, decorative arts, gardens, natural resources, and related subjects.Attributes:Organized and adaptable, with strong project-management skills and the ability to work independently, manage multiple programs and schedules, and respond to changing deadlines and needs.An effective communicator, with strong writing, teaching, facilitation, and public speaking skills and the ability to engage children, youth, families, and educators.Collaborative and relationship-oriented, building productive connections with schools, community partners, colleagues, volunteers, families, and the public.Creative, curious, and resourceful, developing hands-on, developmentally appropriate experiences for different ages, learning styles, abilities, and needs.Patient, approachable, and professional, exercising sound judgment, diplomacy, and composure when working with minors and managing group dynamics.Committed to inclusive, accessible, and welcoming learning experiences that respond to learners with diverse backgrounds, abilities, learning styles, and needs.The Work Environment:Youth and student learning at the MSV takes place across the campus and in the community. You may teach a school group in a gallery, facilitate a Makerspace activity, welcome families to a hands-on program, lead an educator workshop, or bring Museum learning to a school or community setting.Work in galleries, classrooms, the Makerspace, event spaces, historic areas, gardens, outdoor spaces, schools, and community locations.Interact regularly with children, youth, educators, families, and groups; move throughout Museum spaces and stand or walk for extended periods during programs.Set up, move, or prepare program materials and audiovisual equipment.The essential functions of this position must be performed with or without reasonable accommodation.Your Schedule:This is a full-time, exempt position with a 40-hour workweek and eligibility for hybrid work. Work is performed primarily during daytime hours, Monday through Friday, with evening and weekend availability required as needed.Daily schedules may vary based on programming, meetings, events, and operational needs. On-site availability is required for program delivery, collaboration, and interaction with Museum audiences and partners. Remote work arrangements require supervisor approval and follow MSV’s Hybrid & Remote Work Policy.Benefits:Medical, life, and disability insurance.A 403(b) employer contribution of 5% of annual salary after one year of employment.Paid vacation leave, sick leave, and holiday time.Complimentary individual or family MSV membership and individual Virginia Association of Museums (VAM) membership.Reduced membership costs at Valley Health Wellness & Fitness Center.Daily access to the MSV’s gardens, museum galleries, and more than three miles of fully accessible trails.Why Work at the MSV?The MSV’s mission is to preserve and enrich the cultural life and heritage of the Valley. Located in Winchester, Virginia, its 214-acre campus brings together museum galleries, the Glen Burnie House, seven acres of gardens, and The Trails at the MSV, a free-admission art park.As Manager of Youth & Student Learning, you’ll help young people connect with this special place through experiences that encourage curiosity and discovery. You’ll join a diverse, energetic, and talented team and contribute to an inclusive, equitable, and accessible community where people feel a sense of belonging.If you enjoy inspiring young learners, building relationships with schools and families, and creating engaging educational experiences, we would love to hear from you.

jobs.title: Program Facilitator at Girl Scouts of the Green and White Mountains
jobs.description: Employer: Girl Scouts of the Green and White Mountains Expires: 11/28/2026 Paid Program Facilitator Position Overview The Paid Program Facilitator plays a key role in delivering the Girl Scout Leadership Experience to girls participating in GSGWM Programs. The Paid Program Facilitator is responsible for coordinating the day-to-day operation of the troop, ensuring that meetings are organized and engaging, attendance and documentation are accurate, supplies are prepared, and communication between the co-leader, families, partner site, and GSGWM staff is consistent and effective. The Paid Program Facilitator serves as the primary point of contact for the troop and works collaboratively with all Troop Leaders to create a safe, inclusive, and positive Girl Scout experience. Provide a Safe and Inclusive Environment • Ensure the physical and emotional safety of all girls during meetings, activities, events, and field trips. • Follow all GSGWM, GSUSA, and site-specific safety guidelines, policies, and procedures. • Create an inclusive environment where every girl feels welcomed, respected, and valued. • Follow all rules, policies, procedures, and expectations established by the partner organization. • Communicate safety, behavioral, or other concerns promptly to the appropriate site contact and GSGWM staff. Lead Troop Meetings • Facilitate Girl Scout meetings. • Ensure meetings follow the Girl Scout Leadership Experience and approved Girl Scout curriculum. • Plan activities that support badges, Girl Scout program areas, leadership development, and girl-led experiences. • Use available Girl Scout Experience Boxes and other council resources to support meeting planning. • Coordinate meeting responsibilities with the Co-Leader. • Ensure all necessary supplies and materials are gathered and prepared prior to each meeting. • Arrive 15–30 minutes prior to the scheduled meeting time to prepare the meeting space and materials. • Ensure the meeting space is cleaned and returned to appropriate condition following the meeting. Attendance & Record Keeping • Take accurate attendance at every troop meeting. • Submit attendance according to GSGWM procedures and deadlines. • Monitor attendance patterns and communicate prolonged absences or withdrawals to GSGWM staff. • Maintain accurate records of girl participation, badges, patches, uniforms, and other program activities. • Ensure required membership, permission, and health documentation is completed and submitted. Communication & Coordination • Serve as the primary point of contact for the Co-Leader regarding troop activities and responsibilities. • Maintain regular communication with the Co-Leader between meetings as needed. • Communicate regularly with GSGWM staff regarding troop progress, attendance, behavior concerns, supplies, upcoming activities, and staffing needs. • Participate in scheduled check-ins with GSGWM staff. • Communicate important information from the GSGWM staff to the Co-Leader and caregivers. • Maintain professional and timely communication with site staff and families. • Communicate schedule changes, cancellations, special events, and other important information to the appropriate individuals. Supply & Material Management • Review upcoming lessons and activities in advance. • Gather and organize all supplies needed for meetings. • Maintain an organized inventory of troop supplies. • Communicate supply needs to GSGWM staff in advance. • Coordinate with the Co-Leader regarding preparation of materials. • Coordinate with the partner site regarding available storage space. • Ensure Girl Scout supplies and materials are properly stored and cared for. Behavior & Girl Support • Establish and reinforce positive behavior expectations. • Address routine behavioral concerns using Girl Scout and site-approved practices. • Work with the partner site's staff when the Girl Scout program operates within an afterschool program and additional behavioral support is needed. • Communicate ongoing or significant behavioral concerns to GSGWM staff. • Support girls in developing conflict resolution, communication, teamwork, and problem-solving skills. Badges, Patches, Uniforms & Service • Track badges and patches earned by girls. • Follow current GSGWM guidelines for ordering and distributing badges and patches. • Coordinate uniform distribution and maintain accurate records. • Ensure troop activities include opportunities for service and Take Action projects. • Provide at least one Take Action or community service project per membership year when applicable. Events & Field Trips • Communicate upcoming Girl Scout events, field trips, and special activities to the Co-Leader and caregivers. • Assist with required permission forms and documentation. • Prepare girls for participation in events and field trips. • Ensure attendance and required documentation are completed for off-site activities. Financial & Cookie Program Responsibilities • Follow all GSGWM financial policies and procedures. • Support participation in the Girl Scout Cookie Program. • Complete required Cookie Program training. • Communicate Cookie Program information and deadlines to families. • Assist with parent/guardian communication and required permissions. • Maintain accurate cookie inventory and financial records as assigned. • Ensure all Cookie Program activities follow GSGWM and GSUSA policies. • Communicate cookie-related questions or concerns to GSGWM staff. Collaboration with the Co-Leader • Clearly communicate weekly responsibilities and expectations. • Share lesson plans, supplies, schedules, and program updates. • Work as a team to ensure continuity when one facilitator is absent. • Support the Co-Leader in understanding Girl Scout procedures and expectations. • Maintain a positive and respectful professional relationship. Professional Expectations • Complete all required background checks and Girl Scout training. • Attend required meetings, trainings, and professional development opportunities. • Provide excellent customer service to girls and families. • Communicate professionally and effectively with families, site staff, the Co-Leader, and GSGWM staff. • Represent Girl Scouts positively in the community. • Uphold the Girl Scout Promise and Law. • Serve as a positive role model for girls. Goal of the Role The Program Facilitator ensures that the Girl Scout Troop is organized, prepared, well communicated, and operating in accordance with Girl Scouts of the Green and White Mountains and partner-site expectations while creating an engaging and empowering experience for every girl.

jobs.description: Employer: Hagerstown Community College Expires: 11/28/2026 SUMMARY STATEMENTThis full-time, tenure-track faculty position is responsible for providing high-quality, accessible instruction and supporting student success through excellence in teaching, professional development, scholarship, and service. Faculty members are expected to contribute to the mission and strategic goals of Hagerstown Community College (HCC) through instruction, assessment, curriculum development, student mentorship, shared governance, and community engagement. As exempt employees, faculty have an expected work week of 37.5 hours and maintain a significant campus presence during the 10-month contract period. The faculty member serves within the Behavioral and Social Science and contributes to the ongoing development, assessment, and continuous improvement of the Substance Abuse Counseling concentration. The position includes responsibilities related to student learning outcomes assessment, curriculum development, adjunct faculty support, and institutional service. ORGANIZATIONAL RELATIONSHIPSA. Faculty reports directly to the Division Director of the Behavioral and Social Science. B. Faculty collaborates with the Division Director, Behavioral and Social Science faculty, other division colleagues, student support personnel, and other college stakeholders. FACULTY ESSENTIAL RESPONSIBILITIESA. TEACHING –A faculty member is expected to prepare for and teach an assigned instructional load (15 credits in the fall and spring terms) with a minimum of 5 office hours per week. As part of their teaching duties, faculty are expected to:1. Utilize effective instructional activities and strategies that support learning outcomes and promote effective engagement for student learning and achievement.2. Develop methods of assessment that align with the learning outcomes at the course, program, general education, and institutional levels.3. Utilize assessment results to support continuous improvement of instruction, curriculum, and student success initiatives to submit outcome assessment reports by the required deadlines.4. Contribute to the continuous review, development, and improvement of curriculum. Faculty are expected to incorporate current disciplinary knowledge, emerging technologies, and evidence-based instructional practices into course content and delivery.5. Maintain current course materials in the appropriate learning management repository and updating as needed to align with college expectations and all legal requirements (i.e. federal accessibility, etc.).6. Provide clear effective communication by maintaining accessibility and regular, substantive interaction with students to ensure expectations are clearly conveyed and adequate feedback is provided on academic work.7. Advocate and mentor students by fostering an inclusive learning environment, providing guidance and support as appropriate. Advise students regarding academic progress, program requirements, transfer opportunities, and career pathways by collaborating with appropriate college personnel (Advising, Learning Support Services, Career Services, Workforce Development, etc.).8. Maintain accurate records of attendance and scholastic performance and submit all requirements (i.e. financial aid attendance, midterm/final grades, etc.) by required deadlines.B. SCHOLARSHIP AND PROFESSIONAL DEVELOPMENT - A faculty member engages in ongoing professional development to maintain disciplinary expertise, enhance instructional effectiveness, support scholarship, and contribute to institutional priorities. Examples include but are not limited to:1. Attending required New Faculty onboarding and training (i.e. New Faculty Orientation/Group Meetings, D2L/Technology training, Quality Matters, Teaching in the Community College).2. Attending conferences, seminars or workshops that have received prior approval from appropriate administrative areas.3. Creating professional works or publications (i.e. articles, books, art or music performances, etc.).4. Completing relevant graduate coursework or other professional trainings, internships, practical field work, etc.5. Other projects such as reviewing or editing publications, participating in professional organization discussions or peer partnerships projects. C. SERVICE – the extent to which a faculty member provides college or community service is factored into promotion criteria and should align with the strategic goals and mission of the college. Examples include but are not limited to:1. Participation through service on departmental, divisional, and institutional committees (i.e. search committee, program review, accreditation, ad hoc or other shared governance groups.2. Provide guidance and support to adjunct faculty to promote consistency in curriculum implementation, assessment practices, instructional quality, and student learning outcomes in alignment with the College's mission and goals.3. Contribute to promotion of the College’s mission and strategic plan through the provision of time or expertise/advisement for programming, initiative development and student-oriented activities for outreach, enrollment and retention (i.e. Unit Planning, grants, Open House/Career Fair events, etc.),4. Serves as an ambassador for the College and their discipline by participating in activities that support and sustain partnerships between the college, community and external groups to promote community engagement or outreach. FACULTY PROGRAM SPECIFIC RESPONSIBLITIES D. Supervise required internships E. Chair the program’s Advisory CommitteeF. Seek out and maintain close relationships with local agencies that work with Substance Abuse clients EDUCATION AND EXPERIENCEA Masters degree is required within the appropriate discipline. SKILLS AND ABILITIESPreference will be given to candidates with recent teaching experience at the undergraduate or community college level. Candidates must possess strong organizational, advising, and interpersonal skills, with a demonstrated ability to communicate effectively with students, faculty, staff, and administrators. Strong instructional and classroom management skills are required.

jobs.title: High School AP Environmental Science Teacher at Henderson Collegiate
jobs.description: Employer: Henderson Collegiate Expires: 11/28/2026 Do you have a passion for science? Are you interested in helping students master science and critical thinking skills that will set them up for college and beyond? Henderson Collegiate has an opening for a High School AP Environmental Science Teacher.The AP Environmental Science teacher will be responsible for preparing students for the AP exam through a hands-on curriculum aligned to the AP curriculum. Each science teacher at Henderson Collegiate is assigned an instructional coach to help you navigate the complexities of leading a classroom and teaching rigorous content. In addition to being observed by your coach regularly, you would also meet with them one on one to help develop your teaching skills and close student gaps in understanding. Science teachers are encouraged to incorporate hands-on learning experiences, including project based learning, experiments that use the scientific method, and application based exercises with data sets. To further support you as a science teacher, you would be part of a school-wide science department that ensures continuity as students progress from year to year to help students develop the skills and habits that set them up for success in upcoming science courses and in college.Applicants should have a bachelor's degree, but do not need a degree in education. Salary ranges between $48,000 and $86,000 depending on level of education and experience. This is an immediate opening for our 2026-27 school year.Who We AreHenderson Collegiate is a mission-driven public college preparatory school located in rural Henderson, NC with an unrelenting focus on character development and student achievement. We believe in 51% character and 49% academics, as we will never sacrifice a moment to teach our students character traits that will help them become great people.Our school serves students that come from traditionally underserved communities (approximately 85% receive free or reduced-price meals, and about 94% are students of color). However, we consistently rank in the top 9.7% of all NC schools and the top 1.3% of all NC Title I schools. Henderson Collegiate is committed to the idea that all students can learn and create a future for themselves that is full of opportunities. We know they can do this by attending and graduating from the colleges of their choice. Our students are proving what is possible and to date, 100% of our seniors have been accepted into a 4-year college or university.We are both a team and family who leverage passionate people to be the best teachers and leaders that they can be. We believe in the idea that all of our staff members are school teachers, as opposed to classroom teachers, meaning that no matter your role, we are all willing to do whatever it takes to support all Henderson Collegiate students. We work together to make what most people say is impossible, happen.Who You AreA go-getter that will move mountains to do what is best for our students and team An encourager who knows that with learning comes joy, love and laughter A reflective educator who recognizes the power and potential within all students and strives to provide them with culturally competent/responsive instruction A life-long learner that continuously strives to be a better version of themselves through learning, improving and being hungry for feedback A gritty problem-solver who approaches challenges with smart solutions in mind A finisher who plans backwards to meet timelines and manage complex projects and who keeps in mind both the big picture and the details necessary to make things happen A data-driven analyst who reflects and takes swift action based on results A proactive communicator who reaches out to students, families, and teammates What You’ll DoBring it. Have stamina and the ability to set and achieve ambitious goals, and handle the intensity required to bring your best self to an extended school day in a very high-performing school environment. Own and develop your own content and curriculum. Do the intellectual preparation needed to create and develop rigorous assessments, unit plans, lesson plans, and instructional materials; demonstrate expertise in and a genuine passion for curriculum that is contagious to students. Deliver strong. Dynamically lead students in whole-class and small-group settings, cultivate intellectual curiosity and a love of learning in students, and adjust instruction using qualitative and quantitative data to ensure student understanding and meet differentiated student needs. Reach higher – and sweat the small stuff. Develop, uphold, and implement Henderson Collegiate’s values, policies, and systems to effectively manage a classroom and consistently lead students to meet sky-high academic and character-based expectations. Never stop growing. Offer and receive constructive feedback from colleagues in order to create a professional working atmosphere that aspires to excellence and is conducive to constant improvement; dive humbly into school-wide and individual professional development, including pre-service training over the summer and weekly sessions during the academic year. Spread the love. Build deep relationships with students, families, and staff to foster a culture of joy and community. Maintain strong lines of communication with families about student progress, and go above and beyond to support and collaborate closely with teammates in the united pursuit of Henderson Collegiate’s mission. The Fine PrintRequired: All candidates must have a Bachelor’s degree. Preferred: Prior experience teaching and working in a low-income community is preferred but not required. Benefits: Salary is competitive and commensurate based on experience, our teacher pay scale can be found here. Additionally, Henderson Collegiate offers a full benefits package. Teachers receive a laptop computer and are provided with classroom technology and software. We believe in going the extra mile for students and as a result our school day is longer than many other schools. The school day for staff is from 7:20 am to 4:15 pm, with one day a week staff being expected to stay until 5:00pm for professional development. At this time we are not able to sponsor candidates who are looking for an initial US work visa.

jobs.title: Middle School Teacher at Henderson Collegiate
jobs.description: Employer: Henderson Collegiate Expires: 11/28/2026 Are you interested in helping students in grades 5-8 master foundational skills that will set them up for success in high school and beyond? Henderson Collegiate is looking for candidates interested in becoming a Middle School Teacher to join our team for the upcoming school year. While we don't yet know our exact subject needs for the 2027-28 school year, we want to start speaking with awesome candidates like yourself who are already exploring their options for next year. In the application, you will have the opportunity to share your content area preferences.Each teacher at Henderson Collegiate is assigned an instructional coach to help you navigate the complexities of leading a classroom and teaching rigorous content. In addition to being observed by your coach regularly, you would also meet with them one on one to help develop your teaching skills and close student gaps in understanding. To further support you as a teacher, you would be part of a school-wide content specific department that ensures continuity as students progress from year to year to help students develop the skills and habits that set them up for success in upcoming math courses and in college.Applicants should have a bachelor's degree, but do not need a degree in education. Salary ranges between $48,000 and $86,000 depending on level of education and experience. This is an opening for our 2027-28 school year and new teachers will begin in mid July.Who We AreHenderson Collegiate is a mission-driven public college preparatory school located in rural Henderson, NC with an unrelenting focus on character development and student achievement. We believe in 51% character and 49% academics, as we will never sacrifice a moment to teach our students character traits that will help them become great people.Our school serves students that come from traditionally underserved communities (approximately 85% receive free or reduced-price meals, and about 94% are students of color). However, we consistently rank in the top 9.7% of all NC schools and the top 1.3% of all NC Title I schools. Henderson Collegiate is committed to the idea that all students can learn and create a future for themselves that is full of opportunities. We know they can do this by attending and graduating from the colleges of their choice. Our students are proving what is possible and to date, 100% of our seniors have been accepted into a 4-year college or university.We are both a team and family who leverage passionate people to be the best teachers and leaders that they can be. We believe in the idea that all of our staff members are school teachers, as opposed to classroom teachers, meaning that no matter your role, we are all willing to do whatever it takes to support all Henderson Collegiate students. We work together to make what most people say is impossible, happen.Who You AreA go-getter that will move mountains to do what is best for our students and team An encourager who knows that with learning comes joy, love and laughter A reflective educator who recognizes the power and potential within all students and strives to provide them with culturally competent/responsive instruction A life-long learner that continuously strives to be a better version of themselves through learning, improving and being hungry for feedback A gritty problem-solver who approaches challenges with smart solutions in mind A finisher who plans backwards to meet timelines and manage complex projects and who keeps in mind both the big picture and the details necessary to make things happen A data-driven analyst who reflects and takes swift action based on results A proactive communicator who reaches out to students, families, and teammates What You’ll DoBring it. Have stamina and the ability to set and achieve ambitious goals, and handle the intensity required to bring your best self to an extended school day in a very high-performing school environment. Own and develop your own content and curriculum. Do the intellectual preparation needed to create and develop rigorous assessments, unit plans, lesson plans, and instructional materials; demonstrate expertise in and a genuine passion for curriculum that is contagious to students. Deliver strong. Dynamically lead students in whole-class and small-group settings, cultivate intellectual curiosity and a love of learning in students, and adjust instruction using qualitative and quantitative data to ensure student understanding and meet differentiated student needs. Reach higher – and sweat the small stuff. Develop, uphold, and implement Henderson Collegiate’s values, policies, and systems to effectively manage a classroom and consistently lead students to meet sky-high academic and character-based expectations. Never stop growing. Offer and receive constructive feedback from colleagues in order to create a professional working atmosphere that aspires to excellence and is conducive to constant improvement; dive humbly into school-wide and individual professional development, including pre-service training over the summer and weekly sessions during the academic year. Spread the love. Build deep relationships with students, families, and staff to foster a culture of joy and community. Maintain strong lines of communication with families about student progress, and go above and beyond to support and collaborate closely with teammates in the united pursuit of Henderson Collegiate’s mission. The Fine PrintRequired: All candidates must have a Bachelor’s degree. Preferred: Prior experience teaching and working in a low-income community is preferred but not required. Benefits: Salary is competitive and commensurate based on experience, our teacher pay scale can be found here. Additionally, Henderson Collegiate offers a full benefits package. Teachers receive a laptop computer and are provided with classroom technology and software. We believe in going the extra mile for students and as a result our school day is longer than many other schools. The school day for staff is from 7:20 am to 4:15 pm, with one day a week staff being expected to stay until 5:00pm for professional development. At this time we are not able to sponsor candidates who are looking for an initial US work visa.

jobs.description: Employer: College Living Experience Expires: 11/28/2026 Young Adult Transition ProgramJob Type: Part-timeHours: Approximately 15-32 hours per weekWork Location: In person – San DiegoStart Date: ASAPPay: $19-$22 per hour Are you looking for a job where your work truly matters, every day is different, and you get to be part of a fun and supportive community? At College Living Experience (CLE), academic success isn't built through grades alone. It happens during study sessions, conversations with professors, time-management planning, problem-solving challenges, and the everyday moments where students learn how to navigate college with greater confidence and independence. As an Academic Coach, you'll help neurodiverse young adults discover how they learn best and develop the skills needed to succeed in college and beyond. You'll work alongside students to strengthen executive functioning, organization, study habits, self-advocacy, and academic confidence while helping them navigate the challenges of higher education.We are looking for someone who is patient, creative, and passionate about helping students reach their potential and succeed in college-level. Someone who enjoys mentoring, adapting their approach to different learning styles, and celebrating growth along the way. Candidates often come from backgrounds in education, tutoring, special education, academic coaching, psychology, student support services, learning assistance, or humanities instruction. Current areas of need include:Environmental ToxicologyPhysical AnthropologyProgramming FundamentalsSocial Media ToolsComputers in HospitalityGeneral computer/technology courseworkWriting, English, literature, history, communications, philosophy, and political science Teachers, tutors, graduate students, adjunct instructors, and professionals with relevant subject-matter expertise are encouraged to apply. In this role, you'll provide individualized academic coaching and tutoring, help students develop effective study strategies, manage assignments and deadlines, communicate with professors, prepare for exams, and build the skills needed to become more independent learners. You'll collaborate closely with our social, career, and independent living teams to ensure students receive holistic support across all areas of their development.The ideal candidate believes that success looks different for every student and is excited to help neurodiverse young adults build confidence, overcome challenges, achieve their educational goals, and create a strong foundation for lifelong learning and independence. Why People Love Working at CLE Working at CLE means being part of a collaborative team dedicated to helping students achieve meaningful academic and personal growth. Every day is different. You'll work one-on-one with students, helping them navigate college coursework, develop effective learning strategies, and overcome challenges that may be impacting their success. You get to see real progress. One of the most rewarding aspects of this role is watching students gain confidence, improve their academic skills, and become more independent learners. You can be creative in your approach. No two students learn the same way. You'll have the flexibility to adapt strategies, develop individualized supports, and find innovative ways to help students succeed. You build meaningful relationships. Academic coaching at CLE goes beyond tutoring. You'll serve as a mentor, guide, and advocate as students navigate their college experience. You're part of a supportive team. Our academic, career, social, and independent living staff work closely together to provide holistic support and celebrate student successes. Academic Coaching & Executive Functioning Support Provide individualized academic coaching and tutoring based on each student's learning style, strengths, and academic goals. Review syllabi, assignments, grades, and course requirements to help students create realistic semester and weekly plans. Teach and reinforce executive functioning skills, including organization, time management, prioritization, task initiation, and study strategies. Help students prepare for exams, complete projects, and develop effective note-taking and learning techniques. Support students in communicating with professors, academic advisors, and campus Disability Support Services (DSS) when appropriate. Foster self-advocacy, problem-solving, and independent learning skills. Communicate concerns, successes, and recommendations to the Academic Coordinator and interdisciplinary team. Maintain accurate records and support student goal tracking throughout the semester. Strong organizational and problem-solving abilities Ability to work both independently and collaboratively within a team environment

jobs.description: Employer: Trinity Christian Academy of Cape Cod Expires: 11/28/2026 T R I N I T Y C H R I S T I A N A C A D E M Y O F C A P E C O D Dean of StudentsReports To Head of School Employment Full-time Location Barnstable, MA Term 12-month · Year-round WHO WE ARE Trinity Christian Academy (TCA) of Cape Cod is an accredited Christian school serving students from Pre-Kindergarten through High School. TCA is committed to academic excellence within a distinctly Christian environment where students are known, valued, challenged, and encouraged to grow in faith, character, and relationship with Christ. OUR MISSION Charting a course of lifelong learning and leading through Christian Education. POSITION SUMMARY The Dean of Students plays a pivotal role in cultivating a Christ-centered school culture where students are supported and challenged to grow spiritually, academically, socially, and in character. The Dean provides leadership in student life, fostering a positive school environment grounded in biblical values, personal responsibility, mutual respect, and accountability. Working collaboratively with the Head of School, faculty, staff, students, parents, churches, and community partners, the Dean oversees student leadership development, discipline, attendance, and wellness. Through biblical principles, restorative practices, sound judgment, and clear communication, the Dean promotes student growth, strengthens relationships, and helps cultivate a community where students are equipped to make wise choices that reflect Christ in their daily lives. QUALIFICATIONS Education & Credentials • Bachelor’s degree in Education, Counseling, Seminary, Leadership/Ministry, Christian Counseling, or a related field (Master’s degree preferred). • Willingness to complete Dean of Students training/certification within the first year and pursue additional student-services and/or HR training as appropriate. Experience • Five or more years of relevant professional experience, with pastoral, ministry, Christian school, counseling, or student leadership experience strongly preferred. • Experience working with students, families, and/or ministry communities and building positive culture. • Understanding of child and adolescent development and spiritual, social, and emotional needs of students. Faith Commitment • A personal, active Christian faith and a lifestyle consistent with Trinity Christian Academy’s statement of faith and standards, including active participation in a local church. • Demonstrates Christlike character, models biblical values, and is willing to lead prayer, devotions, and faith-based decision-making. SKILLS & PERSONAL CHARACTERISTICS • Excellent communication skills, active listening, empathy, discretion, and conflict-resolution skills. • Builds trust and maintains positive, professional relationships. • Calm, organized, resilient, teachable, and able to manage competing priorities. • Identifies individual student needs and develops practical, thoughtful, and mission-aligned responses. • Ability to lead discipline and conflict mediation in a biblical, ethical, consistent, and restorative manner. KEY RESPONSIBILITIES • In the absence of the Head of School, assume designated responsibilities and provide leadership for the daily operations of the school. • Partner with the Head of School to foster a safe, respectful, Christ-centered school culture and promote TCA’s core values. • Build authentic relationships with students, parents/guardians, and faculty/staff. • Collaborate with the TCA chaplain to plan and execute the annual chapel program, high school retreat, and other opportunities for spiritual growth while cultivating relationships with local pastors and churches. • Lead student discipline, behavioral documentation, and restorative conflict resolution, including intentional communication with students, families, and faculty. • Develop and oversee student wellness and leadership programs that support students’ spiritual, emotional, social, and personal growth. • Coordinate and oversee the Uniform Code and recommend revisions as appropriate. • Address individual student needs in partnership with faculty, families, and the Head of School, to provide appropriate spiritual, emotional, behavioral, and practical support. • Develop programs and resources to educate and support parents on student spiritual growth, emotional health, and behavior. • Support TCA’s accreditation standards related to student well-being and spiritual growth and collaborate across departments to implement related initiatives. • Other duties as assigned by the Head of School. WORK ENVIRONMENT & PHYSICAL REQUIREMENTS This position works in a standard school environment and requires a regular on-campus presence during school hours and at select evening and weekend events. The role involves moving about campus throughout the day and responding to the active demands of a school setting. Reasonable accommodations will be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions of the role. COMPENSATION & BENEFITS Salary range: $55,000 – $60,000, commensurate with experience and qualifications. Benefits include life insurance, tuition benefits, paid time-off, and professional development support. This is a full-time, 12-month position. TO APPLY Interested candidates should submit a cover letter, current résumé, personal statement of Christian faith, and three professional references, including one pastoral reference, to Suzanne Powers at spowers@tcaofcc.org as soon as possible, and no later than December 1, 2026. The Academy does not unlawfully discriminate on the basis of race, color, national origin, sex, age, or disability in its employment practices.

jobs.title: Chemistry Lab Technician at Stefanini
jobs.description: Employer: Stefanini Expires: 11/28/2026 Stefanini Group is hiring for Chemistry Lab Technician in Plymouth, MN for a medical Device Client!You can share your resume directly at sahnaj.pervin@stefanini.comContract Length: 12+ monthsMax pay: $26/hr on W2, biweekly paymentCandidate must be comfortable to work 8 hours per day Summary The Testing Laboratory Technician performs laboratory testing on fluid/process samples to detect and quantify cellular and particulate targets and to differentiate true signals from common interferents (e.g., red blood cells (RBCs), fungal elements, and lipids). The role is responsible for accurate sample handling, instrument operation, and complete data logging so results can be grouped and trended by sampled material, fluid tube sizing, and sample aging. Key ResponsibilitiesReceive, label, and process fluid/process samples in accordance with written procedures and chain-of-custody requirements. Prepare samples and run testing to detect and/or quantify cellular and particulate targets using approved methods and instrumentation. Identify and document potential interferents and artifacts (e.g., RBCs, fungal elements, lipids) and apply established criteria to distinguish them from true target signals. Perform routine instrument setup, calibration/verification checks, and basic troubleshooting; document out-of-spec conditions and escalate per procedure. Maintain accurate, complete, and contemporaneous laboratory records (paper and/or electronic) including calculations, raw data, and observations. Support method improvements by capturing atypical findings, suggesting refinements to decision criteria, and participating in investigations as assigned. Maintain a clean and organized workspace; stock consumables and maintain inventory levels needed to support scheduled testing. Data Logging & Sample Grouping Requirements Log sample identifiers and collection metadata (date/time, source, operator, volume, and any deviations) to ensure traceability. Capture results and classification details (e.g., counts/estimate, confidence flags, and notes) and separately record interferent observations (RBC presence, fungal forms, lipid droplets/particulates) using standard terminology. Ensure data are entered in the approved format so results can be filtered, compared, and summarized across the required groupings. Record sample descriptors needed for grouping / trend analysis, including such things as: Sampled material (e.g., product/contact material, process condition, or collection location as defined by the lab). Fluid tube sizing (e.g., tubing inner diameter/size category and configuration, if applicable). Sample aging (e.g., time from collection to test, storage conditions, and number of freeze/thaw or hold steps if used).Qualifications Associate degree or higher in laboratory science, biology, chemistry, medical laboratory technology, or equivalent experience. 1+ years of laboratory experience preferred (sample handling, wet lab techniques, or analytical testing); entry-level candidates with strong lab coursework considered. Comfortable working with biological fluids and following biosafety practices. Strong attention to detail with demonstrated ability to document work clearly and follow written procedures. Basic computer proficiency for data entry and file management (LIMS/ELN experience preferred). Work Environment & Compliance Work is performed in a laboratory setting that may require use of personal protective equipment (PPE). Follow Good Documentation Practices (GDP) and applicable quality system requirements (e.g., GLP) as defined by the organization. May require standing, repetitive pipetting/bench work, and handling of small containers and tubing components. Schedule may include time-sensitive testing based on sample collection windows and sample aging requirements.

jobs.description: Employer: Hudson River Housing/Middle Main Expires: 11/28/2026 Housing Care Manager - May's HousePoughkeepsie, NYDescription Hudson River Housing improves lives and communities through housing with compassion and development with vision. We are dedicated to building strong, sustainable communities by developing and preserving quality affordable housing and helping families and individuals obtain and maintain housing through education, advocacy and support services. We are a committed group of people from all backgrounds who care deeply about our community and want to make it a better place. Position: Housing Care Manager – May’s House General Description: The Care Manager is responsible for providing services to families and individuals in their assigned program. These services may include providing general information about program, crisis intervention services, developing comprehensive goal-oriented service plans, providing an appropriate level of guidance and support, facilitating referrals, and serves as advocate on behalf of participant to assist them in securing services, entitlements and support to reach their goals. Principal Duties: 1. Providing general information about program, crisis intervention services, and may screen or participate in the screening of applicants for acceptance into program. 2. Orienting participants to program and conducting intake interviews to collect information and assess the needs and strengths of program participants. 3. Developing comprehensive goal-oriented service plan in conjunction with program participant and where appropriate their family members, service providers and/or significant others. 4. Providing an appropriate level of guidance and support to assist participants in meeting basic needs, addressing their service plan goals, overcoming challenges and coping with disappointment. 5. Facilitating referrals and serves as advocate on behalf of participant to assist them in securing services, entitlements and support to reach their goals. 6. Sharing information with other program staff members and collaborating with outside service providers to ensure participants holistic needs are addressed in a coordinated manner. 7. Providing individual, group and family counseling in accordance with goals and participants’ case plan. 8. Facilitating or arranging for facilitation of workshops, support groups and other activities to help participants develop living skills, increase interpersonal relations and support systems, maintain healthy life styles and enrich their lives. 9. Monitoring participants’ compliance with program rules and requirements, intervening to stabilize crisis situations and delivering positive and negative consequences in accordance with program procedures. 10. Monitoring progress toward service plan goals at regular intervals establishing new goals and strategies as needed. 11. Participating in applicant interviews, case reviews, staff meetings, training sessions, supervisory meetings, committee meetings, agency events, and other activities as directed. 12. Monitoring confidential participant files, case notes, records and reports as requested. 13. Assisting participants in preparing for discharge, developing a discharge and/or aftercare plan, and maintaining agreed upon follow-up contact. 14. Providing general office support, operation support, and assistance with general program management when necessary and as directed. 15. Participating in planning efforts to evaluate program’s effectiveness, identify needs and trends, and develops strategies to overcome challenges and enhance program quality. 16. Obtaining ongoing training as required and as necessary to effectively perform duties and provide professional growth. Qualifications: Education/Knowledge: BA/BS in human service field or equivalent combination of education, training and experience. Experience: Two years related work experience with youth population. Must have competent reading and writing skills along with strong communication skills. Required Behaviors: Must have excellent organizational skills and have the ability to prioritize the demands of the job. Must demonstrate sensitivity toward the Program’s target population, and ability to comfortably and effectively relate to individuals of diverse backgrounds, and be respectful of cultural differences. Must be responsible, non-judgmental able to work independently and as part of a team. Must have a strong commitment to personal and professional ethics and standards and be able to set and maintain appropriate boundaries with Program participants. Must be dependable and flexible. License Requirements: Valid NYS Driver’s License required. Physical Demands: Must be able to climb multiple sets of stairs. Helen Keller Services for the Blind is thrilled to announce we will be expanding our Children's Learning Center to two brand-new Long Island locations in Nassau and Suffolk County! These state-of-the-art facilities will serve preschool children who are blind or have low vision, as well as multiple disabilities, autism, Down syndrome, or pervasive developmental delays. This expansion reflects HKSB’s commitment to ensuring that Long Island families have access to the same high-quality early education and support services that have transformed lives in our Brooklyn Children Learning Center. We currently have an exciting opening for a Teacher of the Visually Impaired (TVI) in our soon to open Suffolk County Preschool! Located in Islandia, NY, the Teacher of the Visually Impaired/ Special Education Teacher will conduct a special education preschool classroom for children with an Individualized Education Plan (IEP). Specific responsibilities will include: Utilize diverse and engaging curriculums to maximize students’ learning opportunities and promote active participation within the classroom.Develops and implements student specific adaptations for sensory, motor, self-help, and other areas of need in collaboration with therapists to maximize whole child learning approach for each student.Conducts functional vision assessments and learning media assessments (as appropriate within program scope) and integrates findings into daily instruction to ensure students access curriculum through appropriate visual, tactile, and auditory modalities.Implements and oversees instruction in areas such as compensatory access skills (e.g., braille readiness, tactile discrimination), assistive technology, and sensory efficiency, ensuring these are embedded throughout the instructional day in alignment with each student’s IEP.Leads the selection, adaptation, and ongoing use of specialized materials and equipment (e.g., braille, large print, tactile symbols, optical devices), and ensures classroom staff are trained and consistently implementing these supports to maintain full access to instruction for students with visual impairments.Establishes and maintains relationships with families to further the development of the child by assisting the family to carry over strategies from school to home. Acts as the primary contact between home and school; maintaining the liaison with school social worker daily.Accurately monitors and records progress toward IEP goals while providing clear direction and oversight to staff to ensure consistent and reliable data collection.Continuously evaluates student progress and documents that progress in report cards, progress notes and annual updates.Submits weekly lesson plans and newsletters to the Principal.Maintains accurate attendance documents, submits to the administrative assistant monthly.Advocates for the educational and developmental needs of their students both in the school and in the wider community.Attendance at all student IEP meetings; annuals along with reconvene opportunitiesDevelop and maintain strong rapport with school district representatives. Participates in teacher and team meetings and completes tasks from those meetings in a timely and professional manner.Actively participates in school wide functions such as field trips, graduation, parent days, etc.Seeks out and participates in professional development activities, appropriate to the population of students, both within the school and in the larger educational community. Assist in the training and mentoring of new staff as well as peer-to-peer training situations.Plans, assigns, and monitors instructional assistant responsibilities and schedules to promote seamless classroom operations and student support.Prepares and delivers annual reviews for classroom teaching assistants.The TVI will complete all required trainings within the first six months of employment and all other required trainings throught the course of their employment with HKS.QualificationsValid New York State teaching certification in one of the following:NYS Students with Disabilities (Birth–Grade 2), orNYS Students with Disabilities (All Grades), orOther NYSED special education certification(s) approved to be the teacher of record in a 4410 preschool settingValid New York State certification as a Teacher of Students Who Are Blind or Visually Impaired (TVI)*Bachelor’s degree from an accredited college or university required, Master’s Degree preferred (including NYS required pedagogical coursework in early childhood education and teaching students who are visually impaired)Ability to implement IEPs and deliver specially designed instruction in accordance with NYSED and CPSE expectationsProficiency in Microsoft Office and ability to use school-based systems for documentation, communication, and recordkeeping.Prior experience preferred in preschool special education, including implementation of IEPs and participation in CPSE and multidisciplinary team meetings to support each student's educational and developmental needs.*Only candidates who hold a New York State Teacher of the Visually Impaired (TVI) certification, or who are actively in the process of obtaining NYS certification through the Office of Teaching Initiatives, will be considered for this position. CERTIFICATES, LICENSES, REGISTRATIONS Valid New York State Students with Disabilities (Birth-2nd Grade or All Grades)Valid New York State certification as a Teacher of Students Who Are Blind or Visually Impaired (TVI)Physical Demands: The employee must frequently lift and/or move up to 40 pounds.At HKS we strive to provide a healthy work-life balance for our employees. We offer generous paid time off and comprehensive benefit package including: Paid Time Off (in accordance with the school calendar), Paid Personal Time and Paid Sick TimeHealth Benefits Package including Medical, Dental and Vision coverageHealthcare Flexible Spending Accounts Life Insurance and Disability benefitsVoluntary Ancillary Benefits 403 (b) Savings Plan with company match Employee Assistance ProgramHelen Keller Services for the Blind is an equal opportunity employer.
